title: Safety of Flight - Weather Services and Hazards
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 7 covering aviation weather services, products, and flight hazards

cards.back:
Flight Service: 1-800-WX-BRIEF
Online: www.1800wxbrief.com
AWC: aviationweather.gov

Types of briefings:
• Standard - Complete, planning
• Abbreviated - Update/supplement
• Outlook - 6+ hours out

Example: KORD 121856Z 27015G25KT 3SM RA BKN010 OVC025 18/16 A2992

KORD: Airport
121856Z: Day/time (UTC)
27015G25KT: Wind 270° at 15, gusting 25
3SM: Visibility 3 statute miles
RA: Rain
BKN010: Broken at 1,000'
OVC025: Overcast at 2,500'
18/16: Temp/dewpoint
A2992: Altimeter 29.92

Example: TAF KORD 121720Z 1218/1324 28012KT P6SM SCT030...

KORD: Airport
121720Z: Issued day/time
1218/1324: Valid 18Z day 12 to 24Z day 13
28012KT: Wind
P6SM: Visibility > 6 SM
SCT030: Scattered at 3,000'

Change groups: FM, TEMPO, PROB, BECMG

VFR: Ceiling >3,000' AND visibility >5 SM

MVFR (Marginal VFR): Ceiling 1,000-3,000' AND/OR visibility 3-5 SM

IFR: Ceiling 500-<1,000' AND/OR visibility 1-<3 SM

LIFR (Low IFR): Ceiling <500' AND/OR visibility <1 SM

AIRMET Sierra (S):
• IFR conditions
• Mountain obscuration

AIRMET Tango (T):
• Moderate turbulence
• Strong surface winds (>30 kts)
• Low-level wind shear

AIRMET Zulu (Z):
• Moderate icing
• Freezing levels

Issued for weather hazardous to ALL aircraft:

• Severe icing (not associated with thunderstorms)
• Severe or extreme turbulence/CAT
• Dust/sandstorms reducing visibility <3 SM
• Volcanic ash

Valid: 4 hours (6 for volcanic ash/tropical cyclone)

Issued for convective hazards:

• Tornadoes
• Lines of thunderstorms
• Thunderstorms with heavy precipitation (≥40% of area)
• Embedded thunderstorms
• Severe thunderstorms with:
 - Surface winds ≥50 kts
 - Hail ≥3/4 inch
 - Tornadoes

UA (routine) Or UUA (urgent)
/OV Location
/TM Time (UTC)
/FL Flight level or altitude
/TP Aircraft type
/SK Sky conditions
/WX Weather
/TA Temperature
/WV Wind
/TB Turbulence
/IC Icing
/RM Remarks

ALWAYS report:
• Icing (any intensity)
• Turbulence (moderate or greater)
• Wind shear/LLWS
• Volcanic ash

Also helpful:
• Cloud tops and bases
• Visibility
• Conditions differing from forecast
• Good weather (confirms forecast)

LIGHT: Slight, erratic altitude/attitude changes

MODERATE: Aircraft control remains positive but occupants feel strain against belts

SEVERE: Large, abrupt changes; aircraft may be momentarily out of control

EXTREME: Aircraft practically impossible to control; structural damage possible

TRACE: Barely perceptible, not hazardous

LIGHT: Rate allows extended flight, deicing/anti-icing manages it

MODERATE: Rate of accumulation requires diversion

SEVERE: Rate is such that deice/anti-ice fails to reduce hazard; immediate exit required

CLEAR ICE:
• Large supercooled droplets
• Smooth, hard, glossy
• Difficult to remove
• Most hazardous

RIME ICE:
• Small supercooled droplets
• Rough, milky, opaque
• Lighter, easier to remove

MIXED: Combination of both

CUMULUS (Building):
• All updrafts
• 15-25 min

MATURE (Most Dangerous):
• Updrafts AND downdrafts
• Rain, hail, lightning
• 15-30 min

DISSIPATING:
• Mostly downdrafts
• Light rain
• Anvil spreads

• Don't fly under a thunderstorm
• Stay 20 NM from severe storms
• Don't fly between cells if <2/3 apart
• Don't rely solely on onboard radar
• Avoid flying into anvil cloud
• If penetration unavoidable:
 - Fly straight through (shortest path)
 - Maintain attitude, not altitude
 - Slow to maneuvering speed

MICROBURST:
• Intense localized downdraft
• <1 mile diameter, 5-15 min duration
• Downdraft >6,000 fpm possible
• Wind changes of 45+ kts

Survival:
• Add power, pitch up
• Don't try to maintain altitude
• Escape the shear envelope

Pressure altitude corrected for temperature

High density altitude = thin air = reduced performance:
• Less lift
• Less engine power
• Longer takeoff roll
• Reduced climb rate

Worst: Hot, High, Humid
(3 H's of hazard)

Visual indicators:
• Lenticular clouds (lens-shaped)
• Cap clouds over peaks
• Rotor clouds (turbulent)

Hazards:
• Severe turbulence in rotor zone
• Downdrafts on lee side
• Can exceed aircraft climb rate

Cross ridges at 45° angle for escape

RADIATION: Clear nights, light winds, cools ground
ADVECTION: Warm moist air over cold surface
UPSLOPE: Air rises along terrain
STEAM: Cold air over warm water
PRECIPITATION: Rain falling through cold air
ICE: Supercooled droplets, temps below -25°F

Most common: Radiation & Advection

COLD FRONT:
• Fast-moving, steep slope
• Short duration, intense weather
• Cumuliform clouds, T-storms possible

WARM FRONT:
• Slow-moving, shallow slope
• Prolonged weather, gradual change
• Stratiform clouds, steady precip
• Wider area of IFR conditions

At sea level:
• Temperature: 15°C (59°F)
• Pressure: 29.92 in Hg (1013.25 mb)
• Lapse rate: 2°C per 1,000 ft

Why it matters:
• Calibration of instruments
• Performance charts based on std atm
• Density altitude calculations

Generated by all aircraft, worst:
• Heavy, clean, slow aircraft
• Sinks at 400-500 fpm
• Levels off ~900 ft below flight path

Avoidance:
• Stay above/upwind of heavy aircraft path
• Rotate before their rotation point
• Land beyond their touchdown point
• Wait 3 min (same runway) or 2 min (parallel)

Peak times: Dawn, dusk, spring/fall migration

High-risk areas:
• Near water
• Landfills, grain areas
• Wildlife refuges
• Below 3,000 AGL

If strike occurs:
• Assess damage
• Return to airport if able
• Report bird strikes to FAA

Volcanic ash is EXTREMELY hazardous:
• Abrasive - damages windscreen
• Can cause engine failure
• Clogs pitot/static systems
• Electrical failures

If encountered:
• Reduce thrust
• Exit area immediately
• Descend to warmer air if possible
• Squawk 7700, report

Ground-based sensors around airport

Detects:
• Wind shear between sensors
• Microburst signatures

ATC reports:
• 'Microburst alert [location]'
• Wind shear with loss/gain info

Pilot action: Delay takeoff or landing until clear

Online at aviationweather.gov/gfa

Provides:
• Ceiling/visibility forecasts
• Clouds, precipitation
• Icing, turbulence, winds
• 3,000 ft increments to 48,000 ft
• Observed and forecast data
• 14 hours past to 15 hours future

Issued every 6 hours for:
3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 30, 34, 39, 45, 53 thousand feet

Format: DDff+TT
• DD = wind direction (tens of degrees)
• ff = wind speed (knots)
• TT = temperature (°C)

Example: 2714-08 = 270° at 14 kts, -8°C

Light/variable: 9900

Issued by CWSU (Center Weather Service Unit)

• Unscheduled advisory
• Valid up to 2 hours
• Conditions affecting ARTCC airspace

Warns of:
• Conditions meeting SIGMET criteria
• Conditions below SIGMET but significant
• Rapidly developing weather

Turbulence above 15,000' not associated with clouds

Causes:
• Jet stream shear zones
• Strong temperature gradients
• Mountain waves at altitude

Indicators:
• Near jet stream (>100 kt winds)
• Sharp troughs
• High lapse rates

Often no visual warning

Can occur: 20-70°F with visible moisture or high humidity

Most dangerous: 50-70°F (fuel vaporization cooling effect)

Symptoms:
• RPM drop (fixed pitch)
• Manifold pressure drop (constant speed)
• Engine roughness

Prevention: Carb heat as required

When temperature and dewpoint converge:

Small spread (<5°F):
• High humidity
• Fog/low clouds likely
• Expect visibility reduction

Watch for spread closing:
• Indicates moisture condensing
• Fog may form rapidly
• Plan for alternates

Large supercooled droplets that freeze on impact

More hazardous because:
• Accumulate rapidly
• Form behind protected surfaces
• Affect control surfaces
• Can overwhelm deice equipment

SLD conditions:
• Look for freezing rain/drizzle
• Exit immediately if encountered

HIGH PRESSURE:
• Descending air
• Generally fair weather
• Clockwise flow (NH)

LOW PRESSURE:
• Rising air
• Clouds, precipitation likely
• Counter-clockwise flow (NH)

Wind flows from high to low
Fronts separate pressure systems

Types:
• QNH: Local altimeter (airport elevation when on ground)
• QNE: Standard (29.92 / 1013.25)
• QFE: Field elevation (reads zero on ground)

Rule: High to low, look out below!
(Flying into lower pressure without resetting = true altitude lower than indicated)

Continuous broadcast of:
• SIGMETs
• Convective SIGMETs
• AIRMETs
• Urgent PIREPs
• Center Weather Advisories

Broadcast on selected VOR/NDB frequencies

Indicated by 'H' next to NAVAID on charts

Issued during briefing when:
• Current or forecast conditions questionable for VFR
• IFR conditions present/expected
• Mountain obscuration likely

NOT a prohibition!
• Final go/no-go decision is PILOT's
• FSS specialist expressing concern
• Carefully consider the warning
